TS0010001.message: This document declares version '{got}', which this build cannot read.
TS0010001.solution: Write one of the supported versions: {supported}. A version is supported for two further minor releases after its successor ships.

TS0010002.solution: Remove it, or run `tapstate explain` to see the fields allowed here.

TS0010003.solution: It is valid elsewhere but not in this position; run `tapstate explain` to confirm.

TS0010004.solution: Add '{field}' to that block. It has no default, and nothing else in the document implies it.

TS0010005.message: Reference '{ref}' at {path} points to nothing in this workspace.
TS0010005.solution: Define the referenced resource '{ref}', or select an existing resource at {path}.

TS0010006.message: Reference '{ref}' at {path} is ambiguous across more than one source.
TS0010006.solution: Qualify the table with its source, e.g. `source.table`.

TS0010007.message: Field '{field}' at {path} is not allowed for mode '{mode}'.
TS0010007.solution: Remove the field, or change the source mode to one that supports it.

TS0010008.message: Source '{source}' is read by pipeline '{pipeline}' but declares no {path}.
TS0010008.solution: Add '{path}:' to '{source}', saying how it is read. A source named only as a sync or push target supplies a connection rather than rows, and correctly declares none.

TS0010009.message: Value '{value}' at {path} is not allowed; expected {expected}.
TS0010009.solution: Use one of the accepted values.

TS0010010.solution: Fix the CEL expression; only the row envelope fields are in scope.

TS0010011.solution: Review how the resources are wired together.

TS0010012.solution: Ids must be unique within the workspace; rename one of them.

TS0010013.message: Connector '{connector}' does not support mode '{mode}' at {path}.
TS0010013.solution: Choose one of the connector's supported modes: {allowed}.

TS0010014.message: Config field '{field}' of connector '{connector}' at {path} has the wrong type; expected {expected}.
TS0010014.solution: Provide a value of the expected type.

TS0010015.message: Required config field '{field}' of connector '{connector}' is missing at {path}.
TS0010015.solution: Provide the field, or choose a connection mode that makes it unnecessary.

TS0010016.message: Config field '{field}' of connector '{connector}' at {path} has an invalid value '{value}'.
TS0010016.solution: Use one of the allowed values: {allowed}.

TS0010017.solution: Fix the YAML syntax; the line and column point at the problem.

TS0010018.message: Variable '{name}' is not set, and the reference to it gives no default.
TS0010018.solution: Set '{name}' in the environment you apply from, or give the reference a fallback with the $\{var:NAME:default\} form.

TS0010019.message: Reference '{ref}' is not a form the grammar defines.
TS0010019.solution: A reference names a variable, as in $\{var:NAME:default\} for one with a fallback; a lone dollar sign is ordinary text.

TS0010020.message: Expression `{expr}` at {path} reads row fields, but source `{source}` has no discovered schema.
TS0010020.solution: Discover the source before applying this: run `discover-schema {source}`.

TS0010021.message: Expression `{expr}` at {path} computes on column `{column}` of table `{table}`, which is {type} and cannot be computed on without losing what it holds.
TS0010021.solution: Compute on a column whose type survives the operation, or carry `{column}` through unchanged instead of computing on it.

TS0010022.message: Expression `{expr}` at {path} reads column `{column}` of table `{table}`, which nothing resolved a type for.
TS0010022.solution: Whether this expression can run is unknown; drop the reference to `{column}`, or read a column whose type the source declares.

TS0010023.message: The sync at {path} upserts table `{table}` of source `{source}`, but that table declares no key, so no write can be matched to the row it belongs to.
TS0010023.solution: Give `{table}` a primary key and discover `{source}` again, or write with `write_mode: append`, which adds rows instead of matching them. A unique index is not enough: only a primary key is read as the key here.

TS0010024.message: The unwind step `{step}` at {path} names nothing that varies from one element to the next, so every row it expands out of a row would carry that row's own key and the target would keep only the last of them.
TS0010024.solution: Add `element_key` naming a field inside each element that identifies the row it becomes, or `include_array_index` to carry each element's position in the array and be told apart by that.

TS0010025.message: The unwind step `{step}` is written by sync `{sync}`, whose {path} appends rows instead of matching them, so deleting a row would append the elements it used to hold instead of taking their rows away.
TS0010025.solution: Write that sync with `write_mode: upsert`, the default, so the expanded rows can be matched and removed; or serve the unwind to a sync that upserts and keep the append target on output that does not expand.

TS0010026.message: Sync element at {path} of '{resource}' writes through connector '{connector}', which this release does not support as a write target.
TS0010026.solution: Point that element at a source on one of the supported write connectors: {supported}. Reading through '{connector}' is unaffected: the restriction is on what '{source}' is written to, not on what it can be read from.

TS0010027.message: Unwind option `{option}` generates column `{column}`, but that name is already in use.
TS0010027.solution: Choose a name distinct from the parent columns, the array path, and the other generated column. Rename a parent column in an earlier map if necessary.

TS0010028.message: The join SQL at {path} is not valid SQL: {detail}
TS0010028.solution: Fix the SQL; the line and column in that message count from the start of the `sql:` block itself.

TS0010029.message: The join SQL at {path} uses {shape} at line {line}, column {column}, which this release does not run.
TS0010029.solution: A join is one SELECT over tables combined with equality conditions, publishing one row per match; it cannot filter, sort, cut, de-duplicate, aggregate or nest queries. Rewrite the SQL within that subset, or do the rest in a later step.

TS0010030.message: Join `{step}` at {path} reads step `{ref}` through alias `{alias}`, but a join can only read source tables.
TS0010030.solution: Point `{alias}` at the source table the step reads, and do the step's work after the join instead. A join resolves its SQL against the discovered columns of each input and keys its rows on the driving table's primary key; a step's output has neither.

TS0010031.message: Join `{step}` at {path} binds alias `{alias}` to the pattern `/{pattern}/`, but a join input must name one source table.
TS0010031.solution: Write the table's name instead of a pattern, for example `{alias}: orders`. A join reads one table per alias: its SQL names that table's columns and its rows are keyed on that table's primary key. A pattern names a set that can change, so it is refused even where it matches a single table today.

TS0010032.message: Pipeline {pipeline} sets {setting}, which no longer decides anything; nothing reads it.
TS0010032.solution: Remove {setting} and set {instead} on each node that should run differently. A node that sets nothing runs at its node type's default.

TS0010033.message: Source {source} asks to be read by {requested} processors; one processor reads it.
TS0010033.solution: No connector has declared a split read yet, so a source is read by one processor whatever is written. Remove the parallelism, or leave it; nothing else changes.

TS0010034.message: Rollup field `{field}` at {path} names `{function}` as its function; a rollup field names exactly one of {known}.
TS0010034.solution: Write one function key with its argument, for example `{field}: \{ sum: $amount \}`. The qualifiers `filter`, `type` and `default` go beside it.

TS0010035.message: The embed at {path} is `as: {as}` and holds at most one row, so it cannot carry rollup fields.
TS0010035.solution: Read the row's columns directly, or declare the embed `as: array` (or `as: rollup` when the rows should not be shown) if it gathers many rows.

TS0010036.message: The embed at {path} is `as: rollup` but declares no `rollup:` fields, so it would be held and never shown.
TS0010036.solution: Add the fields to compute over it under `rollup:`, or declare it `as: array` to render its rows.
